Key Terms:
Slack Variable: A variable added to a less-than-or-equal-to inequality constraint to transform it into an equality constraint. Vertex: A point where two or more constraint boundaries intersect in the feasible region of a linear programming problem.  In higher dimensions, it is the intersection of multiple constraint hyperplanes.<L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 5><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 6><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 29>

Largest-Increase Rule: A pivot rule in the Simplex method that selects the entering variable that produces the largest increase in the objective function value.<L[2024-09-05-SimplexEfficiency] 6><L[2024-09-05-SimplexEfficiency] 7><L[2024-09-05-SimplexEfficiency] 8>

Klee-Minty Example: A worst-case example for the Simplex method, demonstrating that the number of iterations can grow exponentially with the problem size.<L[2024-09-05-SimplexEfficiency] 2><L[2024-09-05-SimplexEfficiency] 3><L[2024-09-05-SimplexEfficiency] 4><L[2024-09-05-SimplexEfficiency] 5>

Bland's Rule: A pivot rule in the Simplex method designed to prevent cycling, which selects the entering variable with the smallest index among those with positive coefficients and the leaving variable with the smallest index.<L[2024-09-05-SimplexEfficiency] 10>

Smoothed Complexity: A framework for analyzing the complexity of algorithms where the input is perturbed by small random amounts.  It aims to explain the practical efficiency of algorithms even when worst-case examples exist.<L[2024-09-05-SimplexEfficiency] 11>

Randomized Pivot Rule: A pivot rule that randomly permutes the order of variables before applying a deterministic rule like Bland's rule.<L[2024-09-05-SimplexEfficiency] 10>

Interior-Point Method: A class of algorithms for linear programming that traverse the interior of the feasible region, in contrast to the Simplex method which follows the boundary.<L[2024-09-05-SimplexEfficiency] 12>
Primal Problem: A linear programming problem in its standard maximization form, aiming to maximize a linear objective function subject to linear inequality constraints and non-negativity constraints. <L[2024-09-12-Duality] 1><L[2024-09-12-Duality] 2><L[2024-09-12-Duality] 3><L[2024-09-12-Duality] 4>

Dual Problem: A linear programming problem derived from the primal problem, typically in minimization form, with constraints and objective function related to the primal problem through matrix transposition and sign changes. <L[2024-09-12-Duality] 1><L[2024-09-12-Duality] 2><L[2024-09-12-Duality] 3><L[2024-09-12-Duality] 4>

Weak Duality: A theorem stating that for any feasible solutions to both the primal and dual problems, the objective function value of the primal problem is always less than or equal to the objective function value of the dual problem. <L[2024-09-12-Duality] 2>

Strong Duality Theorem: A theorem stating that if a linear programming problem has an optimal solution, then its dual problem also has an optimal solution, and the optimal objective function values of both problems are equal. <L[2024-09-12-Duality] 11><L[2024-09-12-Duality] 17><L[2024-09-12-Duality] 18><L[2024-09-12-Duality] 19><L[2024-09-12-Duality] 20>

Negative Transpose Property: The property that the coefficient matrix of the dual problem is the negative transpose of the coefficient matrix of the primal problem. This property is preserved throughout the simplex method iterations. <L[2024-09-12-Duality] 6><L[2024-09-12-Duality] 7><L[2024-09-12-Duality] 8><L[2024-09-12-Duality] 9><L[2024-09-12-Duality] 10>

Complementary Slackness: A condition stating that for optimal primal and dual solutions, the product of each primal variable and its corresponding dual slack variable is zero, and the product of each dual variable and its corresponding primal slack variable is zero. <L[2024-09-12-Duality] 5><L[2024-09-12-Duality] 21><L[2024-09-12-Duality] 23>

Simplex Method: Iteratively move from one vertex of the feasible region to another by setting non-basic variables to zero and choosing a new set of (non)basic variables to improve the objective function value. Bland's Rule: Choose the variable with the smallest index among those eligible to enter the basis.<L[2024-09-05-SimplexEfficiency] 10>
